public_rationale: Later reports describe exposures and alleged destructive coding-agent actions. They do not establish a sufficiently verified series of new catastrophic failures after April 27. Counting newly discovered older exposures would also require a different reading of “many more.” No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule. The undefined deadline prevents treating the passage of six months as failure.
limitations: Serious privacy exposure can occur without proof of malicious exploitation, but the data and exposure still need verification.
A broader reading that counts newly discovered older failures could change the assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Many more catastrophic vibe-coding failures involving privacy, security and data loss will occur soon.

statement.excerpt: And I am sure we will see many more catastrophic failures soon enough, involving things like privacy, security and data loss. Already there have been many.
statement.document_title: Dario Amodei, hype, AI safety, and the explosion of vibe-coded AI disasters

our_interpretation: The forecast concerns additional failures of coding agents or AI-generated software after April 27, 2026.
Catastrophic means serious realized privacy exposure, security compromise, or operational data loss; ordinary bugs and unexploited vulnerabilities alone do not qualify.
Many means numerous distinct incidents, not repeated coverage of one event. The speaker supplied no count.
Soon enough provides no latest calendar deadline, so no fixed horizon is imposed.
The words we will see could alternatively include newly discovered failures that began before publication.
criteria.support_condition: Dated, corroborated records establish numerous distinct additional severe failures attributable to coding agents or AI-generated software after publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive development rules out the predicted additional failures. Merely finding few reports by an evaluator-selected date cannot contradict this open-ended forecast.

evidence.explanation: The report describes an alleged recent Claude Code incident involving 48,218 lost files. Its underlying Reddit post was deleted, and the report supplies neither independent verification nor an exact occurrence date.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A corroborated incident series documenting numerous distinct severe failures, their post-April-27 occurrence dates, consequences, and connection to coding agents or AI-generated software. A clarified count and deadline would permit a firmer assessment.
